title: How Steve Jobs ran Pixar and Apple by email: grading milestones, keeping the forest in view, and focus
summary: A set of internal emails from 1997 to 1999 showing Jobs holding teams accountable with honest letter grades, setting a short list of annual milestones to keep sight of the "forest", cutting products like Newton for focus, and celebrating wins by crediting the team. The Macintosh anniversary note restates Apple's purpose: bridge sophisticated technology and ordinary people, at the intersection of technology and liberal arts.

principles.text: Grade yourself honestly against milestones set in advance, including giving yourself F's.
principles.quote: Ship Two Strong Interactive Products – F (but A for getting out)

principles.text: Keep a short list of annual goals so leadership can see the forest and correct course when off track.
principles.quote: The purpose of this list is to remind us of the “forest” from time to time, and to help prod us into taking corrective action when we get off track.

principles.text: Invite criticism of your plans from your senior team before committing to them.
principles.quote: Please feel free to shoot full of holes with your comments.

principles.text: Make hard focus decisions deliberately, stand by them, and treat upset customers with respect.
principles.quote: Our decision to end Newton development was not taken lightly, and is unlikely to be reversed. Even so, let’s welcome the Newton customers and developers who come to protest this decision.

principles.text: Celebrate wins by naming the people responsible and making the achievement human and concrete.
principles.quote: Few people ever get the chance to make 7.5 million people laugh so much and feel so good. Or 450 people at Pixar feel so proud.

principles.text: Apple's purpose is to bridge sophisticated technology and everyday people by making it easy and fun to use, at the intersection of technology and liberal arts.
principles.quote: It’s our job to make complex technology easy to use and fun to use.
